newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - MEHRTENS GETS HURRY-UP FROM AUCKLAND.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - MEHRTENS GETS HURRY-UP FROM AUCKLAND.

text.p: TAURANGA, Aug 6 - Reserve All Black first five-eighths Andrew Mehrtens was given a torrid time as Bay of Plenty lost 58-12 to a young Auckland side in a non-championship rugby match at the Tauranga Domain on Wednesday.

Mehrtens, making a guest appearance for the Bay, was put under pressure by Auckland's relentless loose forwards -- Dylan Mika, Andrew Blowers and Mark Carter in the first half and then Finau Maka and Charles Riechelmann in the second half.

The Canterbury first-five, on the comeback trail from a hamstring injury which cost him his place in the All Blacks' starting 15, kicked four first-half penalties for the home side and was given a searching workout by Auckland's non-stop attacking play.
Auckland ran in two tries in the first half to lead 20-12 at the break and added a further six tries in the second spell.

The five All Blacks in action -- Mehrtens, Carter, Riechelmann, Auckland halfback Ofisa Tonu'u and Auckland fullback Adrian Cashmore -- were all given plenty of game time, with Riechelmann and Mehrtens playing the full 80 minutes.

Another encouraging display for the All Blacks selectors came from flanker Andrew Blowers, who produced a fine 40 minutes. The 1996 All Black is battling back from a stress fracture to his back which has kept him out of rugby for three months.

Bay of Plenty stayed with Auckland for most of the first half thanks to Mehrtens' penalties, but just before the break the visitors stretched their advantage out to eight points thanks to a try from prop Paul Thomson, which was converted by fullback Adrian Cashmore.
Cashmore left the field early in the second half with a calf muscle problem and his replacement, Esera Puleita, scored a try on debut.
Mehrtens was disappointed with his performance, saying he needed to sharpen up his timing.
"It was disappointing in general, but then it was made to look worse because we were playing Auckland," he said.
"If you make mistakes you get punished by them."
While Mehrtens was fairly happy with his fitness, he said he needed more match play.
"My kicking got better after I relaxed but I need to work generally on getting a bit of speed back and I'll have to do some work on it. I just need to sharpen up."
Mehrtens and the Aucklanders who are in the All Blacks squad for Saturday's tri-series test against South Africa at Eden Park will rejoin the New Zealand squad in Auckland tonight.
